# Python Tip: Mutable Defaults

Does your function use `[]` or `{}` as a default?  
That innocent-looking default can leak state between calls.  
Let's learn why—and how to avoid it!  

:::{.python-logo}
:::

:::

:::



<!-- PANEL 2 -->
:::{.tutorial-panel}

## It Looks Harmless

This function appears to create an empty cart when one is not provided.

:::{.code-animation}
```{python}
def add_to_cart(item, cart=[]):
    cart.append(item)
    return cart

ada_cart = add_to_cart("book")
print("Ada:", ada_cart)
```
:::

The first call works exactly as expected.

:::



<!-- PANEL 3 -->
:::{.tutorial-panel}

## The Silent Bug

Now Grace creates a new cart—or at least, that is what we expect.

:::{.code-animation}
```{python}
grace_cart = add_to_cart("pen")

print("Grace:", grace_cart)
print("Ada now:", ada_cart)
```
:::

Both carts contain both items! State leaked between two separate calls.

:::



<!-- PANEL 4 -->
:::{.tutorial-panel}

## Why It Happens

Python creates default arguments once when the function is defined—not each time it is called.

:::{.code-animation}
```{python}
# Both names point to the same default list
print("Same cart:", ada_cart is grace_cart)
```
:::

Every call that omits `cart` reuses and modifies that one list.

:::



<!-- PANEL 5 -->
:::{.tutorial-panel}

## Watch for Mutable Defaults

Lists are not the only danger. Dictionaries, sets, and other mutable objects can also retain changes.

:::{.code-animation}
```{python}
# Avoid mutable defaults like these
def process(items=[]): ...

def configure(settings={}): ...

def collect(values=set()): ...
```
:::

This is one of Python's best-known warts—and an easy bug to miss in code review.

:::



<!-- PANEL 6 -->
:::{.tutorial-panel}

## Use `None` Instead

Use `None` as the default, then create a fresh object inside the function.

:::{.code-animation}
```{python}
def add_to_cart(item, cart=None):
    if cart is None:
        cart = []

    cart.append(item)
    return cart

print("Ada:", add_to_cart("book"))
print("Grace:", add_to_cart("pen"))
```
:::

Now each call gets its own cart.

:::



<!-- PANEL 7 -->
:::{.tutorial-panel}

:::{.center}

## Wrap-Up

Mutable defaults can introduce **silent shared state** between function calls.

When reviewing code—especially generated code—look for `[]`, `{}`, `set()`, or other mutable defaults.

Use `None`, then create a fresh object inside the function!
